interest: Illuminates postwar Japanese industrial adjustment following the loss of essential colonial pulpwood supplies and chemical mills.
overview: This file documents the status, capacity, and administration of Japan's wood pulp and paper manufacturing industries under Allied occupation between November 1946 and August 1948. Centered on SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 56, the collection provides comprehensive surveys of historical production, mill directories, raw material requirements, and pulping technologies, while detailing the severe industrial dislocation caused by the loss of colonial resources in Karafuto, Korea, and Formosa. The records also compile production statistics, foreign trade reviews requested by the U.S. Department of Commerce, and related industry correspondence.
